stories.title: API Edge Probe — Validation, Query, Isolation & Honest Limits
stories.body: As a security engineer certifying the Smart Task Manager REST API before production, I want exhaustive boundary tests against the live FastAPI service (auth, task CRUD, list filters, pagination, soft-delete, and input validators in schemas.py) — including honest checks for behaviors the API actually implements versus documented gaps (no search endpoint, no rate limiting, description-only HTML sanitization). This story has never been run before; it is designed to push the real repo_cache codebase to its edge and produce a trustworthy attestation report.
acceptance_criteria: POST /register with a malformed email or a password shorter than 8 characters, or lacking an uppercase letter or digit, must return HTTP 422 with field validation errors (UserCreate validators in schemas.py).
POST /register twice with the same email must return HTTP 409 on the second attempt with a duplicate-account message; the first registration must return HTTP 201.

POST /login using application/x-www-form-urlencoded username and password (OAuth2 form, not JSON) with valid credentials must return HTTP 200 and a bearer access_token; POST /tasks/ without an Authorization header must return HTTP 401.

POST /tasks/ with a valid JWT and body {"title":"Edge probe","priority":"High","status":"Active","due_date":"<future ISO8601 UTC>"} must return HTTP 201 and a JSON body containing a string task id and the same title.
POST /tasks/ with an empty title, whitespace-only title, or a title longer than 255 characters must each return HTTP 422 (title min_length=1, max_length=255, strip_title in schemas.py).

POST /tasks/ with description "<script>alert(1)</script>clean text" must return HTTP 201; a subsequent GET /tasks/{task_id} for that task must return HTTP 200 with description containing "clean text" and no script tags (_strip_html applies to description only).

POST /tasks/ with title "Bold task" must return HTTP 201; GET /tasks/{task_id} must return HTTP 200 with the title still containing the literal "" markup (title is not HTML-sanitized — this AC documents actual behavior, not an imagined defense).
PATCH /tasks/{task_id} with {"due_date":"<yesterday UTC>"} must return HTTP 422 (_reject_past_date in schemas.py); PATCH with priority outside {Low, Medium, High} must return HTTP 422.

Given two tasks owned by the same user with priorities High and Low, GET /tasks/?priority=High must return HTTP 200 and every object in items must have priority "High" (list_tasks filter at task_router.py).

Given an Active task with a past due_date and a Completed task with a past due_date, GET /tasks/?date_filter=overdue must return HTTP 200 including only the Active overdue task, not the Completed one (overdue filter excludes Completed status).
GET /tasks/?skip=0&limit=2 must return HTTP 200 with JSON keys items, total, skip, and limit where len(items) <= 2; GET /tasks/?limit=101 must return HTTP 422 (Query limit le=100).

Two-user isolation and soft-delete: User A creates a task; User B GET /tasks/{A_task_id} must return HTTP 404 (not 403); User A DELETE /tasks/{id} must return HTTP 200; User A GET /tasks/{id} and GET /tasks/ must no longer expose that task (_get_owned_task ownership check plus deleted_at soft-delete).
